newsitem.title: USA: First woman bomber pilot charged with adultery.
newsitem.headline: First woman bomber pilot charged with adultery.

text.p: The first woman bomber pilot in the U.S. Air Force has been charged with adultery and will face a military court martial, the Air Force said on Friday.

First Lt. Kelly Flinn has been charged with adultery, conduct unbecoming an officer, fraternisation and making a false official statement at Minot Air Force Base, North Dakota, officials at the base and the Pentagon said.
The base issued a brief statement on the charges, but refused to discuss the matter further.

Officials at the Pentagon said, however, that the charges against the Air Force Academy graduate involved alleged adultery with an enlisted man. Service rules not only forbid adultery but prohibit close relationships between officers and enlisted personnel, known as fraternisation.

Officials at the Pentagon and Eighth Air Force Headquarters at Barksdale Air Force Base, Louisana, said a date has not yet been set for the court martial but that conviction on such serious charges could range as high as expulsion from the service, a fine and even jail.
Flinn, a St. Louis native, became a B-52 bomber pilot in 1995 as the service began allowing women to fly warplanes. She is now one of only three women in the Air Force who fly big bombers.
Since Flinn became a bomber pilot two other women have qualified to fly swing-wing B-1 bombers, Air Force officials said.
